title: A Cluster-Based Model of the Spectrum of Erbium-Doped GdVO$_4$
authors: Zachary H. Roberts, Masaya Hiraishi, Luke S. Trainor, Jevon J. Longdell
abstract: Experimental observations of rare-earth ions doped into an antiferromagnetic crystal show an enriched optical spectrum. In this paper we present a cluster-based model to describe erbium ions doped into a gadolinium vanadate (Er:GdVO$_4$) host crystal, wherein the erbium ion couples directly to its four nearest neighbour gadolinium ions, which in turn couple to the mean field of the rest of the crystal. Compared to previous models in the literature, the parameters used to fit this model are fewer in number, with clearer physical origins. Agreement with the experimentally observed optical spectrum of Er:GdVO$_4$ suggests that our model succeeds in capturing the most important interactions of the system, suggesting that it may be useful for predicting microwave-to-optical transduction in future experiments.
summary: The authors present a refined cluster model to describe how rare-earth ion optical spectra are modified by the magnetic environment of their host crystal. By treating only nearest neighbors explicitly, they achieve better parameterization than previous models. This work is significant for predicting quantum phenomena like microwave-to-optical energy transduction in these solid-state systems.
main_problem: To develop a cluster-based model that accurately describes the complex optical spectrum of erbium ions doped into a gadolinium vanadate crystal.
main_result: The proposed cluster model successfully reproduces the experimentally observed optical spectra across various magnetic field regimes, suggesting it captures the essential spin-lattice coupling mechanisms in the material.
method: The authors developed and applied a Hamiltonian incorporating terms for the $	ext{Er}$ ion, the $	ext{Gd}$ lattice spins, and their mutual interactions. They utilized a cluster approximation where only four nearest neighbor $	ext{Gd}$ ions are treated explicitly interacting with the mean field of the bulk crystal.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{Er:GdVO}_4$, involving electronic transitions of $	ext{Er}^{3+}$ coupled to the magnetic excitations (spins) of the $	ext{Gd}^{3+}$ host lattice. The model Hamiltonian includes terms for crystal field, Zeeman effects, and exchange/dipole interactions.
key_observables: Optical transmission spectrum at various applied magnetic fields; specific energy level transitions ($	ext{Z}_1 	o 	ext{Y}_{1,2}$); avoided crossings in the spectra.
important_parameters: Exchange couplings ($J$, $I$), crystal field parameters, and external magnetic field strengths (e.g., 1 T).
main_assumptions: The model employs a cluster approximation treating only four nearest neighbors explicitly; it assumes $	ext{Gd}$ ions have $L=0$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the local environment of the dopant, energy level diagrams showing spin splitting, and comparisons between measured optical spectra (at various misalignments/fields) and model predictions.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the full Hamiltonian ($H = H_{	ext{Er}} + H_{	ext{Gd}} + H_{	ext{Er-Gd}}$), details the cluster approximation for $	ext{Gd}$ spins, presents the fitting procedure using experimental spectra, compares results across different magnetic phases (AFM, SF, PM), and discusses discrepancies with high-field measurements.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics as it models the coupling between electronic transitions ($	ext{Er}^{3+}$) and collective spin excitations ($	ext{Gd}$ spins). The focus on predicting avoided crossings makes it directly applicable to quantum optics and understanding light-matter interactions in magnetic materials.
